payload.name: spectral-crossover
payload.scope: A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying the median energy location across the full spectrum at a given analysis frame — the frequency at which cumulative energy reaches 50 percent of the total — standardized for use in music information retrieval and audio classification.

payload.body: Spectral-crossover is a spectral analysis parameter quantifying the median energy location of a full spectrum at a given analysis frame, unbounded by any sub-band: the frequency at which the cumulative energy reaches 50 percent of the spectrum's total energy. Parameters: (1) the full set of frequency bins i=1..N with center frequencies f_i, (2) the per-bin energy values E_i = |A_i|^2 over the whole spectrum, (3) the analysis frame window. Computed by ordering the bins in ascending frequency, accumulating the per-bin energies until the running total first reaches half of the total energy sum, and taking the center frequency of the bin at that crossing. The value is in hertz: a low crossover means most energy sits below the median frequency (dark spectrum), a high crossover means energy is pushed toward the upper bins (bright spectrum). It is the whole-spectrum counterpart of spectral-band-crossover, which restricts the same cumulative test to bins within [f_low, f_high). It differs from spectral-centroid (energy-weighted mean, sensitive to high-energy outliers) and from spectral-rolloff (the cumulative crossing at an arbitrary threshold such as 85 percent, measuring brightness rather than the median). Being the 50th percentile of the energy distribution, the crossover is robust to heavy-tailed energy. Persistence: the standardized mathematical definition of the full-spectrum energy median in spectral analysis, implemented in audio analysis toolkits and MIR feature pipelines. [formal: medium spectrale | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.name: spectral-evenness
payload.scope: A human-made spectral analysis measure quantifying how uniformly spectral energy is distributed across all frequency bins of a full spectrum at a given analysis frame — the coefficient of variation of the per-bin energies — standardized for use in music information retrieval and audio classification.

payload.body: Spectral-evenness is a spectral analysis parameter quantifying how uniformly energy is distributed across the frequency bins of a full spectrum at a given analysis frame, unbounded by any sub-band: the coefficient of variation of the per-bin energies. Parameters: (1) the full set of frequency bins i=1..N, (2) the per-bin energy values E_i = |A_i|^2 over the whole spectrum, (3) the analysis frame window. Computed as evenness = sigma/mu, where mu = (1/N) SUM E_i is the arithmetic mean of the per-bin energies and sigma = sqrt((1/N) SUM (E_i - mu)^2) is their standard deviation. The value is a dimensionless ratio: 0 when every bin carries identical energy (a perfectly flat spectrum), increasing without upper bound as energy concentrates in fewer bins. Being a ratio of two homogeneous quantities, it is level-invariant: scaling all bin energies by a constant leaves it unchanged. It is the whole-spectrum counterpart of spectral-band-evenness, which computes the same ratio over bins within [f_low, f_high). It differs from spectral-entropy (Shannon information content of the normalized energy distribution, bounded, logarithmic scale) and from spectral-flatness (geometric-mean-to-arithmetic-mean ratio, measuring flatness on a multiplicative scale): evenness is the dispersion of energies normalized by the arithmetic mean on an additive scale. Persistence: the standardized mathematical definition of full-spectrum energy uniformity in spectral analysis, implemented in audio analysis toolkits and MIR feature pipelines. [formal: aequabilitas spectrale | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]

payload.name: per-bin-energy-vector
payload.scope: The ordered tuple of non-negative per-bin energy values from a spectral decomposition, indexed by bin center frequency over a contiguous bin range — the shared substrate operand of full-spectrum and band-restricted spectral descriptors.

payload.name: per-bin-energy-vector
payload.scope: The ordered tuple of non-negative per-bin energy values from a spectral decomposition, indexed by bin center frequency over a contiguous bin range — the shared substrate operand of full-spectrum and band-restricted spectral descriptors.

payload.body: For a spectral decomposition with N frequency bins indexed i=1..N, each with center frequency f_i and complex amplitude A_i, the per-bin energy vector is the ordered tuple v = (|A_1|², |A_2|², …, |A_N|²) of non-negative scalars ordered by bin index, each entry being the energy of its bin. It is parameterized by the decomposition and a bin range [i_min, i_max] within 1..N: at the full range the vector covers all bins of the spectrum; at a range covering exactly the bins whose centers fall in a frequency band [f_low, f_high) it is the band-restricted vector. Persistence mechanism: explicit storage of the ordered tuple as the substrate operand that spectral descriptors read their per-bin energies, means, centroids, and maxima from directly, rather than from any scalar summary. [formal: vector energiae binarum | substrate: mind | horizon: as-long-as-us | explicit: yes | epoch: 0.01]
